steps.title: Gather equipment and consumables
steps.instruction: Collect 50 ml conical tubes (BD 352098 or equivalent), 100 ml graduated cylinder, 100 ml glass beaker, clean magnetic stir bar, stir plate, ice bucket with regular ice, calibrated pH meter, osmometer, 10 ml luer‑lock syringes (BD 309604, 3), 1 N KOH (BDH3212‑1, as needed), Neurobiotin 488 (Vector SP‑1125, 2 mg), and all reagents listed below.

steps.title: Set up beaker and stir bar
steps.instruction: Place the clean stir bar into the glass beaker, set the beaker on the stir plate, and start stirring at ≥400 RPM. Fill the ice bucket with regular ice and keep it ready.

steps.title: Dissolve primary salts
steps.instruction: Measure 50 ml MilliQ water with the graduated cylinder and add it to the beaker. Stir at ≥400 RPM and slowly add 0.0224 g (22.4 mg) KCl, 3.044 g K‑Gluconate, 0.238 g (238 mg) HEPES, and 0.011 g (11 mg) EGTA while stirring. Cover the beaker with clean parafilm while EGTA dissolves. Once fully dissolved, place the beaker in the ice bucket, ensuring the stir bar continues mixing.

steps.title: Add Sodium GTP
steps.instruction: Retrieve Sodium GTP from the freezer, keep on ice, weigh 0.0157 g (15.7 mg), and add it slowly to the beaker while stirring. Continue stirring at ≥400 RPM until all solids are dissolved.

steps.title: Adjust to 100 ml final volume
steps.instruction: Remove the stir bar with a magnetic stir‑bar remover, transfer the solution to a clean, labeled 100 ml volumetric flask, and bring the volume to exactly 100 ml with MilliQ water.

steps.title: Aliquot 30 ml for use
steps.instruction: Using a graduated cylinder, measure 30 ml of the solution into a new beaker containing a stir bar and stir at ≥400 RPM. Transfer the remaining 70 ml into two labeled 50 ml conical tubes and store them in the freezer for future internal‑solution or fluorescence aliquots.

steps.title: Add phosphocreatine, Mg‑ATP, Biocytin
steps.instruction: Retrieve phosphocreatine, Magnesium ATP, and Biocytin (or 2 mg Neurobiotin 488) from the freezer and keep on ice. Slowly add 0.0765 g (76.5 mg) phosphocreatine, 0.0609 g (60.9 mg) Magnesium ATP, and 0.150 g (150 mg) Biocytin to the 30 ml aliquot while stirring. If using Neurobiotin 488, add 0.002 g (2 mg) instead of Biocytin.

steps.title: Adjust pH to 7.3
steps.instruction: Measure the pH of the solution with a calibrated pH meter and add 1 N KOH dropwise until the pH reads 7.3. Remove the stir bar with the magnetic remover.

steps.title: Check and correct osmolarity
steps.instruction: Take a 10 µl sample and measure osmolarity with an osmometer. If the value is not between 280‑290 mOsm, add MilliQ water to lower or sucrose to raise the osmolarity, re‑measure, and confirm the final osmolarity is within the target range.

steps.title: Filter into syringes
steps.instruction: Draw the final internal solution into three 10 ml luer‑lock syringes and attach 0.45 µm filters to each.

steps.title: Store and label aliquots
steps.instruction: Place the three filtered syringes and the two 50 ml stock tubes in a freezer box at –20 °C. Label the box with reagent name, preparation date, preparer’s initials, measured osmolarity, and pH. Note that the 70 ml stock expires after 60 days.

steps.title: Record documentation
steps.instruction: In the reagent preparation notebook, record the preparation date, lot numbers of all components, final osmolarity, pH, and any adjustments made.

steps.title: Clean up and dispose
steps.instruction: Dispose of any excess reagent directly into the municipal sewer system, wash the magnetic stir bar with MilliQ water, and clean all used glassware.

steps.title: Note component concentrations
steps.instruction: For reference, EGTA (Ethylene Glycol‑bis(2‑aminoethylether)‑N,N,N’,N’‑Tetraacetic Acid) is 0.3 mM; Guanosine‑5’‑triphosphate sodium salt hydrate is 0.3 mM in Internal Solution I (0.2 mM in Solution II); Magnesium ATP is 4 mM in Solution I (3.44 mM in Solution II).
